title: Graphs II: Shortest Paths (0-1 BFS, Implicit Graphs)
relevance: High — second ladder after the standard 0-1 / coupon / multi-source / state-Dijkstra sheet; harder CF-style modeling (sparse/implicit grids, company-switch 0-1, SPT surgery, lex objectives, tiled mazes)
company_notes: OA/interview themes: multi-source infection/Wi-Fi (fires/routers/warehouses; farthest/nearest client — Fire Again / Fair); mode-switch travel (same line free, change line/company costs 1 — Snuke subway / Chamber mirrors); grid turn or stroke limits (bishop/rook rays, ≤2 turns, pond-skater strokes); repair / keep-k roads (Edge Deletion / Breaking Good).

phases.goal: Candidate spots hidden shortest-path graphs: two-cost moves, bounded switch/turn/repair, implicit sparse graphs, or multi-BFS/Dijkstra combo asks.

must_hit.point: Recognize 0-1 shortest-path when moves cost only two values (same company / same direction / good road = 0 else 1), not general Dijkstra.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names company-switch, direction-change, or good/bad-road edges and says deque 0-1 BFS, not a priority queue.

must_hit.point: Recognize bounded turn/switch/repair resource or state (e.g. ≤2 turns, company enter, stroke direction) as a state-BFS / 0-1 state graph.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions state like (r,c,dir,turns) or (cell,dir) / (station,company) rather than plain cell BFS.

must_hit.point: Recognize sparse/implicit or infinite tiled graphs that must not be materialized as a full dense grid.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says hash permitted cells, generate neighbors on the fly, or modular tile visit for Infinite Maze-style tiling.

must_hit.point: Recognize asks that are not one distance: edit the SPT, shortest cycle, farthest ignition, or lex min (length, repairs).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Maps the prompt to SPT keep-k / parent surgery, girth BFS, multi-source farthest, or lex Dijkstra.

probes: What signals that this is 0-1 BFS or an implicit shortest-path graph rather than plain BFS or general Dijkstra?
When would you combine several BFS/Dijkstras on the same skeleton instead of one search?

hints.1: Look at edge costs and whether the graph is named explicitly.
hints.2: Two cost values, mode switches, sparse cells, or SPT/lex/cycle asks all hide shortest paths.
hints.3: If costs are only 0/1 use deque 0-1; if too big to build, hash/generate neighbors; if ask is tree/lex/cycle/farthest, plan multi-search or parents.

phases.goal: Candidate picks the right modeling: 0-1 deque, hubs, reverse multi-source, two-end distances, lex keys, SPT parents, or tiled/stroke graphs.

must_hit.point: 0-1 BFS: push_front on weight 0, push_back on weight 1 so the deque stays sorted by distance.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States front for 0, back for 1, and that distances stay nondecreasing like Dial/0-1.

must_hit.point: Prefer hub/virtual nodes (portals, companies, letter teleports) with 0/1 edges over materializing all-pairs cliques.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Attaches real nodes to a company/portal hub instead of connecting every pair in the group.

must_hit.point: Nearest-special-to-every-node: reverse all edges and multi-source seed every special at dist 0.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes reverse graph + all specials pushed at distance 0 before the loop.

must_hit.point: Two-end distances ds[·], dt[·]; candidate added edge / meet uses ds[u]+w+dt[v]; Destroying Roads extends to two paths with overlap care.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Keeps distances from both ends and combines with one added edge or shared middle segment.

must_hit.point: Lexicographic SP: optimize (path_length, secondary) in one Dijkstra via pair keys or packed cost (e.g. fewest bad roads among shortest).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Uses pair comparison or equivalent packed key so length is primary and repairs secondary.

must_hit.point: SPT surgery: store parents while relaxing; on equal dist prefer smaller weight, or keep only k tree edges.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions parents during Dijkstra and tie-break on weight or outputting min(n−1,k) tree edges.

probes: How do you model same-company rides that cost 0 after paying 1 to enter?
How do you get nearest special distance to every node efficiently?

hints.1: Think about whether costs are 0/1 and whether groups share a mode.
hints.2: 0-1 deque; hubs beat cliques; reverse multi-source for nearest specials; parents for SPT asks.
hints.3: push_front/back for 0/1; virtual (station,company); reverse edges seed specials at 0; store parents and lex pair keys when needed.

phases.goal: Candidate can code 0-1 BFS, multi-source seeding, sparse neighbors, parents, and tiled/stroke visitation correctly.

must_hit.point: Implement 0-1 BFS with a deque and prove/explain why distances stay nondecreasing under front/back pushes.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Writes deque loop with 0→front and 1→back and argues order stays sorted by distance.

must_hit.point: Multi-source: push all sources with dist=0 before the loop; avoid k full separate BFS unless labels need separate layers (Fair).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Seeds every source first, then one BFS; calls out Fair-style per-type layers when needed.

must_hit.point: Sparse/implicit grids: hash permitted cells or generate neighbors on the fly; do not allocate N×M when only P cells exist.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Uses a set/map of allowed squares (King's Path style) and enumerates moves without a full matrix.

must_hit.point: Shortest-cycle BFS: skip the parent edge; update with back-edge using dist[u]+dist[v]+1.
must_hit.evidence_hint: BFS from each start, ignore parent, take dist[u]+dist[v]+1 on non-tree back-edges.

must_hit.point: Infinite/tiled maze: visit key (r mod n, c mod m) but accept a second reach from a different tile copy/offset.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Modular visit index plus absolute tile id / first-offset test for forever-reachable.

must_hit.point: Long-stroke grids: model one stroke of up to K as 0-1 BFS on cells with careful first-visit per ray, not O(K) naive edges per cell.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Continues along a direction with 0-cost steps and direction-change 1, tracking ray visitation under large H·W.

probes: Write the 0-1 BFS deque loop and justify the invariant.
How do you BFS on a sparse set of allowed king-move cells?

hints.1: Start from deque pushes and what you store as state.
hints.2: Seed all sources first; hash cells; for cycles skip parent; for tiles store modular visit plus tile offset.
hints.3: 0→push_front, 1→push_back; dist=0 multi-seed; set of permitted squares; girth with dist[u]+dist[v]+1; (r mod n,c mod m) plus second-tile test; stroke as 0-1 rays not O(K) edges.

phases.goal: Candidate justifies why sparse/0-1/stroke models stay feasible and why naive materialization fails.

must_hit.point: Hubs replace dense group cliques so the explicit edge set stays sparse instead of all-pairs within a company/portal group.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Compares clique blow-up to attaching nodes to one virtual hub with 0/1 edges.

must_hit.point: Long-move strokes must avoid O(K) naive edges per cell; use 0-1 ray visitation so large grids (H·W≤1e6) remain workable.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Rejects per-cell K-edge expansion and cites careful ray/deque processing under H·W≤1e6.

must_hit.point: Implicit sparse graphs must not allocate a full N×M matrix when only a permitted subset of cells exists.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says memory/time follow the permitted cell count via hashing, not the full bounding box.

probes: Why is a virtual company hub better than connecting every pair of stations on that company?
What goes wrong if each pond-skater stroke expands to K explicit edges per cell?

hints.1: Compare materialized size to what you actually traverse.
hints.2: Cliques vs hubs; full grid vs hash set; K edges vs 0-1 along a ray.
hints.3: Hub keeps edges linear in incidences; hash only P cells; 0-1 strokes with first-visit per ray under H·W≤1e6.

phases.goal: Candidate avoids wrong algorithm choice, bad multi-source setup, missed parents/lex ties, and tiled false negatives.

must_hit.point: Do not run general Dijkstra for pure 0-1 company/direction/good-bad edges — use deque 0-1 BFS.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Corrects PQ Dijkstra on 0/1 costs to push_front/push_back deque.

must_hit.point: Do not start multi-source by running separate full searches when one joint BFS with all sources at dist=0 suffices.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Pushes every source before the loop unless Fair-style per-label layers are required.

must_hit.point: For SPT / path / useful-edge asks, forgetting parents (or equal-dist smaller-weight tie-break) loses the tree or min-weight SPT.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Stores predecessor edges while relaxing and on ==dist prefers smaller w when required.

must_hit.point: On infinite tilings, treating modular revisit as blocked misses the second-reach-from-different-tile acceptance condition.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Allows the same modular cell if the tile offset differs from the first visit.

probes: What breaks if you Dijkstra a graph whose only weights are 0 and 1?
When is revisiting a modular cell in an infinite maze still progress?

hints.1: Check algorithm fit and what you mark visited.
hints.2: 0-1 needs a deque; multi-source needs joint seeding; SPT needs parents; tiles need offset identity.
hints.3: Replace Dijkstra with 0-1 deque; seed all sources at 0; store parents and min-w ties; accept second tile offset on (r mod n, c mod m).

tradeoffs.strong_answer: When every edge weight is only 0 or 1 (company switch, direction change, good/bad roads), deque push_front/push_back keeps distances sorted; priority-queue Dijkstra is the wrong default.
For portals, subway companies, or letter teleports, attach real nodes to a hub with 0/1 edges instead of connecting all pairs in the group.

tradeoffs.topic: One joint multi-source BFS vs k separate BFS
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Push all sources with dist=0 for one joint search when that suffices; run separate layers only when labels need them (Fair: per good type, then take s nearest).

tradeoffs.topic: Sparse hash / on-the-fly neighbors vs full N×M grid
tradeoffs.strong_answer: If only a permitted subset of cells exists, hash them and generate neighbors; never allocate the full matrix.

tradeoffs.topic: Lex pair / packed cost vs separate passes only
tradeoffs.strong_answer: For (path_length, secondary) goals like fewest bad roads among shortest paths, optimize with pair keys or packed cost in one Dijkstra (then edit off-path edges as in Breaking Good).

gotchas.trap: Using general Dijkstra for company-switch / direction-change / good-bad 0-1 graphs.
gotchas.correction: Use 0-1 BFS: push_front on weight 0, push_back on weight 1.

gotchas.trap: Materializing dense cliques for portals, companies, or teleports.
gotchas.correction: Add virtual hubs and attach real nodes with 0/1 edges.

gotchas.trap: Computing nearest special via forward searches from every node.
gotchas.correction: Reverse all edges and multi-source BFS from every special at dist 0.

gotchas.trap: Asking for a tree/path/useful edges but not storing parents during Dijkstra.
gotchas.correction: Store parents/predecessor edges while relaxing; for Paths and Trees, on equal dist prefer smaller weight; for Edge Deletion keep min(n−1,k) tree edges.

gotchas.trap: Infinite Maze: marking a modular cell visited forever after first touch.
gotchas.correction: Index visits by (r mod n, c mod m) but accept a cell reached from a different tile copy than first seen.

gotchas.trap: Pond-skater / long strokes expanded as O(K) edges per cell.
gotchas.correction: Model a stroke as 0-1 BFS along a ray with careful first-visit, fitting H·W≤1e6.

gotchas.trap: Shortest-cycle BFS counting the parent edge as a cycle.
gotchas.correction: Ignore the parent; update with non-tree back-edges via dist[u]+dist[v]+1.
